source.locator: lines 37-40, explanation following the second-order assignment definition

findings.finding: The explanation omits both relation assignments: a structure's predicate-symbol-to-relation case and an assignment's relation-variable-to-relation case.
findings.controlling_evidence: The immediately preceding definition includes relation variables and the surrounding first-order semantics assigns relations to predicate symbols; terms and atomic formulas require both cases.
findings.required_translation_handling: State both omitted relation cases and add an adjacent OLTESOLSYN-001 disclosure.

findings.finding: The definition uses M both for the structure and for the relation value, producing M as an element of its own structure-relative powerset notation.
findings.controlling_evidence: A relation-variable value must be an n-place relation R on the fixed domain of structure M, exactly as the neighboring object and function substitution clauses distinguish their assigned values from the structure.
findings.required_translation_handling: Rename the relation value to R throughout that clause and add an adjacent OLTESOLSYN-002 disclosure.

source.locator: lines 90-116, universal and existential relation-quantifier satisfaction clauses

findings.finding: Both relation-quantifier clauses use M for the fixed structure and for the quantified relation, obscuring which object is supplied to the relation variable.
findings.controlling_evidence: The clauses range over every or at least one relation R contained in the n-fold domain of the fixed structure M, while satisfaction remains evaluated in M.
findings.required_translation_handling: Rename the quantified relation to R in both clauses and add an adjacent OLTESOLSYN-003 disclosure.

source.locator: lines 181-182, concluding subset choice in the second satisfaction example

findings.finding: The example uses M simultaneously for the structure and for a proper subset of its domain.
findings.controlling_evidence: The same example already names the quantified subset N, so its conclusion requires N to be a proper subset of the domain of structure M.
findings.required_translation_handling: Use N for the proper subset throughout the concluding choice and add an adjacent OLTESOLSYN-004 disclosure.

source.locator: lines 93-102, forward direction of the Count proposition

findings.finding: The forward proof uses M for both the fixed structure and an arbitrary subset of its domain throughout the relation assignment.
findings.controlling_evidence: The proof must quantify over an arbitrary subset S of the domain of structure M and show that closure under the enumerating successor function forces S to equal that domain.
findings.required_translation_handling: Rename the arbitrary subset to S throughout the argument and add an adjacent OLTESOLSYN-005 disclosure.

source.locator: lines 104-122, reverse direction of the Count proposition

findings.finding: The reverse proof uses M both for the fixed structure and for the subset consisting of the finite iterates of f from m.
findings.controlling_evidence: The proof defines a distinct orbit subset S inside the domain of structure M, verifies the antecedent under the assignment X mapped to S, and then derives S equal to the domain.
findings.required_translation_handling: Rename the orbit subset to S throughout the argument and add an adjacent OLTESOLSYN-006 disclosure.
